facts.value: Aave v3.7 (live on Ethereum Core and BNB Chain since 2026-05-29 per official changelog)
facts.note: Official Aave docs changelog, entry 'Aave v3.7' dated 2026-05-29: "Aave v3.7 completes its rollout with deployments to Ethereum (Core, Lido), Polygon, Avalanche, Arbitrum, Base, BNB Chain, Linea, Plasma, and Mantle." Earlier v3.7 entry dated 2026-04-20: "Introduces protocol-level improvements and safety enhancements. Initial deployment on Sonic, Optimism, Gnosis, Scroll, Celo, MegaETH, XLayer, and Ethereum EtherFi markets." The page also lists 'Aave v3 BNB Chain Market' 2024-01-23: "Aave v3 market deploys on BNB Chain." The page does not explicitly say 'currently live', so 'current = v3.7' is an inference from the latest listed v3.x deployment.

facts.value: Aave v3.5 — changelog date 2025-08-07; GitHub release v3.5.0 published 2025-08-07T19:26:36Z at tag commit 6138e1fda45884b6547d094a1ddeef43dcab4977
facts.note: Changelog entry 'Aave v3.5' (2025-08-07): "Enhances protocol precision and safety with improved rounding methods, internal scaled accounting, and enhanced flag logic." Release/tag data from https://github.com/aave-dao/aave-v3-origin/releases and /tags (v3.4.0=d7a64127dbecb944a73670fbe6fba136329d9e15 2025-07-30; v3.6.0=5a230ec82fcb10afc7fe7cffa8978752fb17aa2b 2026-01-08; v3.7.0=cff15de6d1271b0c800fc001f4aea4c263e8a597 2026-08-05). README section header at main: '**-> Aave v3.5 - July 2025**' / '#### Predictable rounding'.

HEAD of default branch `main` when read. README.md line 5 at this commit: "Aave v3.7 complete codebase, Foundry-based." All file-path and storage facts below are at this commit unless a tag is stated.

338 lines. `balanceOf(user)` (L133-138) = `super.balanceOf(user).getATokenBalance(POOL.getReserveNormalizedIncome(_underlyingAsset))`; `totalSupply()` (L141-143) likewise. `using TokenMath for uint256;` (L25). Identical body at tag v3.5.0 (L134-146). Same path exists at v3.5.0.

135 lines. `abstract contract ScaledBalanceTokenBase is MintableIncentivizedERC20, IScaledBalanceToken` (L16). `scaledBalanceOf(user)` returns `super.balanceOf(user)` i.e. the raw `_userState[user].balance` (L39-41); `getPreviousIndex(user)` returns `_userState[user].additionalData` (L56-58); `_mintScaled`/`_burnScaled` store `index.toUint128()` into `additionalData` (L83, L119).
324 lines. Declares `struct UserState` (L55-59) and `mapping(address => UserState) internal _userState;` (L61). Same path at tags v3.3.0, v3.4.0, v3.5.0.

275 lines. `getNormalizedIncome(reserve)` (L39-55): if `reserve.lastUpdateTimestamp == block.timestamp` return `reserve.liquidityIndex`, else `MathUtils.calculateLinearInterest(reserve.currentLiquidityRate, timestamp).rayMul(reserve.liquidityIndex)`. `updateState` sets `reserve.lastUpdateTimestamp = uint40(block.timestamp)` (L99); `_updateIndexes` writes `reserve.liquidityIndex = reserveCache.nextLiquidityIndex.toUint128()` (L226).

116 lines. `uint256 internal constant SECONDS_PER_YEAR = 365 days;` (L15); `calculateLinearInterest(rate, lastUpdateTimestamp)` (L23-31) divides by SECONDS_PER_YEAR; `calculateCompoundedInterest` at L50 and L93.

167 lines. Constants: `WAD = 1e18` (L20), `HALF_WAD = 0.5e18` (L21), `RAY = 1e27` (L23), `HALF_RAY = 0.5e27` (L24), `WAD_RAY_RATIO = 1e9` (L26). Functions: `rayMul` (L64, half-up), `rayMulFloor` (L74), `rayMulCeil` (L85), `rayDiv` (L104), `rayDivCeil` (L114), `rayDivFloor` (L125). The Floor/Ceil variants are what v3.5 introduced for directional rounding.

Not requested but load-bearing: `getATokenBalance(scaledAmount, liquidityIndex)` (L66-70) `return scaledAmount.rayMulFloor(liquidityIndex);` with docstring "Calculates the actual aToken balance from a scaled balance and the current liquidityIndex. The balance is rounded down to prevent overaccounting." This is the function AToken.balanceOf/totalSupply call since v3.5.
328 lines. Declares `struct ReserveDataLegacy` (L9, kept to preserve the `getReserveData()` ABI) and the internal storage `struct ReserveData` (L42-77).

160 lines. Sibling docs exist at docs/3.1 … docs/3.7 (docs/3.7 has Aave-v3.7-changelog.md, liquidation-rounding.md, etc.). Linked from README line 24 '- [Aave v3.5 features](./docs/3.5/Aave-v3.5-features.md)'.

facts.value: AToken balanceOf and totalSupply now round DOWN (scaled -> unscaled); mint rounds down, burn rounds up, transfer scaled amount rounds up
facts.note: Verbatim, section '#### Rounding `down` for aToken balance operations': "`balanceOf` and `totalSupply` are now rounded down. Currently these methods sometimes overaccount by 1 wei, and sometimes underaccount by 1 wei. From now on they will no longer overaccount." Verbatim from '### Changelog': "In the `AToken` contract: The `balanceOf` and `totalSupply` functions now round down (from scaled to unscaled). The `mint` function now rounds down (from unscaled to scaled). The `burn` function now rounds up (from unscaled to scaled). Calculations of a transfer's scaled amount now round up in `AToken` (from unscaled to scaled)." Also: "Historically Aave has used half-up, or so called bankers rounding, for rounding operations." and "The index has 1e27 precision". Event note: "In v3.5, the `value` emitted in `Mint` and `Burn` events now always accurately reflects the difference between the previous upscaled balance and the new upscaled balance. For `AToken` transfers, the `Transfer` event emits the input amount, while the `BalanceTransfer` event emits the precise scaled amount being transferred."

facts.value: struct UserState { uint120 balance; DelegationMode delegationMode; uint128 additionalData; }  // mapping(address => UserState) internal _userState;
facts.note: CORRECTION to the task premise: at main (v3.7) AND at tags v3.5.0 (6138e1f…, L55-61) and v3.4.0 (d7a6412…, L47-51) the struct is `uint120 balance; DelegationMode delegationMode; uint128 additionalData;` — NOT uint128/uint128. Docstring: "UserState - additionalData is a flexible field. ATokens and VariableDebtTokens use this field store the index of the user's last supply/withdrawal/borrow/repayment." Layout inference (Solidity packing): one 256-bit slot per user = low 120 bits scaled balance, next 8 bits DelegationMode enum, high 128 bits additionalData (last liquidity index, ray). Transfer code uses `uint120 oldSenderBalance = _userState[sender].balance;` (L267).

facts.value: struct UserState { uint128 balance; uint128 additionalData; }
facts.note: The uint128/uint128 form the task describes is correct only for v3.3.0 and earlier. The change to 120 bits happened in v3.4: docs/3.4/Aave-v3.4-features.md (same origin commit 8305565…, section 'Token Storage & implementation alignment', L118-124) states: "In practice this means that on `ScaledBalanceTokenBase` the `.balance` storage was changed from 128 to 120 bits." and "the \"freed\" `8` bits are at the end of the current balance and always `0` (except for aAAve where the occupy delegation related storage)" and "the storage is not directly exposed on the token (no interface change)". So a storage-slot reader must mask the low 120 bits for balance; the 8 delegation bits are 0 for USDT/USDC aTokens.

facts.value: struct ReserveData { ReserveConfigurationMap configuration; uint128 liquidityIndex; uint128 currentLiquidityRate; uint128 variableBorrowIndex; uint128 currentVariableBorrowRate; uint128 deficit; uint40 lastUpdateTimestamp; uint16 id; uint40 liquidationGracePeriodUntil; address aTokenAddress; address __deprecatedStableDebtTokenAddress; address variableDebtTokenAddress; address __deprecatedInterestRateStrategyAddress; uint128 accruedToTreasury; uint128 virtualUnderlyingBalance; uint128 __deprecatedIsolationModeTotalDebt; uint128 __deprecatedVirtualUnderlyingBalance; }
facts.note: Confirmed from source: liquidityIndex ('Expressed in ray'), currentLiquidityRate ('Expressed in ray') and lastUpdateTimestamp (uint40, 'timestamp of last update') are all fields of the packed ReserveData struct in Pool storage. Packing inference from declaration order: slot+0 configuration (uint256 map); slot+1 liquidityIndex|currentLiquidityRate; slot+2 variableBorrowIndex|currentVariableBorrowRate; slot+3 deficit(128)|lastUpdateTimestamp(40)|id(16)|liquidationGracePeriodUntil(40); slot+4 aTokenAddress; … . Tag v3.5.0 (6138e1f…, L42-77) has the identical field order for the first 14 fields; the only difference is the 15th field was still named `isolationModeTotalDebt` (renamed `__deprecatedIsolationModeTotalDebt` later). `deficit` reuses the pre-3.2 `__deprecatedStableBorrowRate` slot; `virtualUnderlyingBalance` occupies the slot that in 3.3.0 held `unbacked` (comments in source).

Read `uint256 public constant ATOKEN_REVISION = N;` from src/contracts/instances/ATokenInstance.sol and `uint256 public constant POOL_REVISION = N;` from src/contracts/instances/PoolInstance.sol at each tag. Useful for the epoch design: the v3.5 rounding semantics correspond to aToken revision 4 (v3.5.0) and persist in revision 5 (v3.6.0/v3.7.0); main (8305565…) also has ATOKEN_REVISION = 5, POOL_REVISION = 11.

Official Aave docs AToken page. It states "balanceOf will always return the most up to date balance of the user, which includes their principal balance and the yield generated by the principal balance." It does NOT describe the scaled-balance formula or the v3.5 rounding direction, and it links to source at github.com/aave-dao/aave-v3-origin/blob/main/src/contracts/protocol/tokenization/AToken.sol and .../base/ScaledBalanceTokenBase.sol (unpinned `main`). The docs 'addresses' page (https://aave.com/docs/resources/addresses) shows no addresses in its HTML and only points integrators to the Aave Address Book repository.

open_questions: Chain IDs (expected Ethereum = 1, BNB Smart Chain = 56) were NOT fetched from chainlist.org / official chain docs in this run; confirm before writing them into the requirements doc.

The exact block number / transaction at which the v3.5 (ATOKEN_REVISION 4) and later v3.7 (ATOKEN_REVISION 5) aToken implementations were activated on Ethereum Core and BNB Chain is not in the address book or docs changelog; it must come from the governance payload repos (bgd-labs protocol-v3.5-upgrade style repos / aave-dao/aave-proposals-reports) or from on-chain Upgraded events, which were out of scope here. This block is what the first explicit epoch boundary should be anchored to.

The address book lists DEFAULT_A_TOKEN_IMPL for each chain (BNB 0x7e199Fc666368d95B9EaEfA7D2d8081AcAb74134, Ethereum 0xadC45Df3cf1584624C97338BEF33363BF5b97AdA) but does not state which ATOKEN_REVISION they are; inferring revision 5 (v3.7) from the aave.com changelog rollout entry dated 2026-05-29 is an inference, not a confirmed fact. Cross-check via ATOKEN_REVISION()/getRevision on-chain or an explorer when RPC use is permitted.

The task's stated UserState layout (uint128 balance, uint128 additionalData) is only correct for aave-v3-origin <= v3.3.0. From v3.4.0 onward (including v3.5.0 and current main) it is uint120 balance + 8-bit DelegationMode + uint128 additionalData. If the requirements doc decodes aToken storage slots directly, it must mask the low 120 bits, and handle pre-v3.4 blocks where the low 128 bits were balance (the extra 8 bits are documented to be always 0 for non-aAAVE tokens, so a 120-bit mask is safe in both eras for USDT/USDC).

Slot-offset numbering for ReserveData (e.g. liquidityIndex|currentLiquidityRate in slot+1, lastUpdateTimestamp in slot+3) is derived from Solidity packing rules applied to the declaration order; it was not verified against a compiler storage-layout dump (forge inspect … storage-layout) in this run.

Only the Ethereum 'Core' market (AaveV3Ethereum.sol) was collected; Ethereum Lido and EtherFi markets (separate Pool proxies in AaveV3EthereumLido.sol / AaveV3EthereumEtherFi.sol) were not collected and may or may not be wanted in the epoch design.

BNB USDT and USDC underlying tokens are 18-decimal per the address book (USDT_DECIMALS = 18, USDC_DECIMALS = 18), unlike Ethereum (6). Any balance-normalization logic must not assume 6 decimals for these symbols.

ReserveLogic.getNormalizedIncome uses the half-up rayMul (not rayMulFloor) to grow the index, while AToken.balanceOf applies rayMulFloor on the result via TokenMath.getATokenBalance; replicating on-chain balanceOf off-chain therefore requires both steps in that order. Confirm the exact rounding chain against v3.5.0 ReserveLogic if the epoch targets v3.5 semantics (only main was read for ReserveLogic).

The aave.com docs changelog does not literally say which version is 'currently live'; 'current = v3.7' is inferred from the latest v3.x deployment entry (2026-05-29) naming Ethereum (Core, Lido) and BNB Chain.
